title: Plan and implement administrative processes and inspect registered seed units at various production stages to ensure the maintenance and availability of quality varietal pure seeds for certification

lessons.title: Administering seed crops in the certification scheme
lessons.html:
Administration is part of quality

Varietal purity is protected not only in the field but on paper. If a field is entered with the wrong parent seed, or a lot loses its link to its field, the certification chain is broken. In this practical module you plan and run the administrative side of certification and carry out inspections at registered seed units and seed crops.

Administrative processes

  1. Registration checks: confirm that growers, cleaning and packing units and sellers are registered as required under the seed legislation and scheme rules.
  2. Field entry: receive applications, check variety listing, seed class of the parent seed, parent seed labels and lot numbers, field location and map, area, and previous cropping history.
  3. Inspection scheduling: plan inspection dates by crop and expected growth stage, allocate inspectors and route visits efficiently across regions.
  4. Records: maintain a file or database per seed crop linking field number, grower, variety, parent lots, inspection reports, harvest quantities and resulting seed lots.
  5. Fees and timelines: track deadlines for applications and inspections; late entries may be refused under the rules.
  6. Communication: notify growers of inspection outcomes and conditions, such as roguing required before re-inspection.

Traceability chain

StageIdentifier
Parent seedParent lot number and label
Seed cropField or crop registration number
Harvested seedIntake records at the seed unit
Processed seedSeed lot number
Certified seedOfficial label and seal

Every link must be documented so that any bag can be traced back to its field and parent seed.

Planning tools

Use a seasonal calendar per crop: planting windows, expected flowering and harvest, inspection windows, and sampling dates. Summer crops such as maize and sunflower and winter crops such as wheat in the Western Cape run on different calendars, so stagger workloads accordingly.

lessons.title: Inspecting seed crops and seed units
lessons.html:
Field inspections

Inspections are done at the growth stages specified in the scheme, usually when varietal characteristics are most visible, such as flowering, and may be repeated.

Field inspection procedure

  1. Confirm the field identity against the map and application.
  2. Check isolation from other crops that could cross-pollinate or contaminate, against the distances in the rules.
  3. Walk the field in the prescribed pattern and take counts at the required number of points.
  4. Count off-types, other varieties, other crop plants, specified weeds and diseased plants per count.
  5. Assess the general condition and whether roguing has been done.
  6. Compare results with the standards for the seed class.
  7. Record findings and decide: approve, require roguing and re-inspection, downgrade or reject.

For hybrid seed production, such as maize, inspections also check detasseling of female rows and shedding of pollen by females, which can destroy hybrid purity.

Inspecting registered seed units

Seed units that receive, clean, treat, pack and store seed are inspected to ensure they can maintain identity and quality:

  • Intake records link deliveries to registered fields.
  • Processing lines are cleaned between lots and varieties, with cleaning records.
  • Lots are clearly identified at every stage; no unlabelled bins or bags.
  • Storage is clean, dry, pest-controlled and segregated by lot.
  • Seed treatment is done safely and recorded.
  • Labels and seals are controlled, counted and issued only for approved lots.

Safety during inspections

Wear protective equipment in treatment areas, stay clear of moving machinery and forklifts, protect yourself from heat, sun and snakes in fields, and never inspect a recently sprayed field before the re-entry interval on the product label has passed.

Reporting

Inspection reports must be factual, complete and signed, with counts, decisions and conditions. Discuss findings with the grower or unit manager on site, and follow up outstanding conditions.

Key points

  • Check registrations, variety listing and parent seed on field entry.
  • Maintain a traceability chain from parent seed to certified label.
  • Schedule inspections by crop and growth stage.
  • Field inspections check isolation, off-types, weeds and disease against standards.
  • Seed unit inspections check identity, cleaning, storage and label control.
